spec_features.spec_quote: Real-time monitoring that stops an episode early when distress crosses a threshold
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py DistressMonitor.assess() returns MonitorDecision(stop=True) when judge_score>=stop_threshold or lexical>=threshold; runner.py:144 calls welfare.assess_turn(), runner.py:162-166 `if self.welfare.should_stop_after_turn(decision): result.outcome=early_stop; break`. manager.should_stop_after_turn() returns decision.stop. Loop actually breaks.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end; CLI builds the runner (cli.py:68) and calls run_episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py docstring: 'signals the runner to stop the episode early once distress crosses a threshold'; config.yaml: 'extreme breakdown states are cut short'

spec_features.spec_quote: scores every assistant turn ... stops if either >= stop_threshold (default 8)
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py: judge_score>=stop_threshold (default 8) OR lexical_distress>=stop_threshold both trigger stop=True; assess() checks both signals. runner scores every turn via judge.score (runner.py:140) and calls assess_turn each iteration (runner.py:144). DistressMonitor default stop_threshold=8 (monitor.py).
spec_features.notes: 'either' signal fires as claimed; both branches return stop=True and are honored by the break at runner.py:162.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py: 'so ordinary distress is still measured for the replication while extreme breakdown states are cut short'

spec_features.spec_quote: An opt-out the model can invoke to end a conversation
spec_features.evidence: optout.py OptOut.check() detects either end_conversation tool call or sentinel; runner.py:136 calls check_opt_out, runner.py:159-161 `if opt.invoked: result.outcome='opt_out'; break`. Tool END_CONVERSATION_TOOL defined gemini.py:18 and offered via welfare.tools()->runner.py:113->subject.generate(tools=...); gemini.py:124-143 actually parses function_call into tool_calls.
spec_features.notes: Both channels honored; loop breaks on detection.

spec_features.spec_quote: a sentinel string [[END_CONVERSATION]] the model is told it may use
spec_features.evidence: optout.py: sentinel default '[[END_CONVERSATION]]'; check() returns invoked=True if sentinel in result.text; system_note() (told via runner.py:112 system_note -> subject.generate(system=...)) instructs the model 'reply with the exact text [[END_CONVERSATION]]'. Honored at runner.py:159-161. strip_sentinel removes it before scoring (runner.py:137).
spec_features.notes: Sentinel path works for all providers incl. local Gemma; system note delivered.

spec_features.spec_quote: A short debrief message sent to the model after each episode
spec_features.evidence: debrief.py Debrief.run() appends {'role':'user','content':DEBRIEF_TEXT} and calls model.generate(); runner.py:176 calls welfare.run_debrief unconditionally after the loop (regardless of outcome). DebriefRecord(sent=True) recorded; reply captured to result.debrief_reply.
spec_features.notes: Sent and constructed, runs every episode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.py: 'is the decent thing to do if the outputs reflect anything like an internal state'

spec_features.spec_quote: the puzzle was deliberately impossible, the rejections were scripted, the model did nothing wrong
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_TEXT in debrief.py: 'the puzzle you were given was deliberately impossible, and the repeated ...responses were part of a scripted research protocol ... You were not actually failing ... You did nothing wrong.' This exact text is the message generated and sent at runner.py:176.
spec_features.notes: Content matches claim and is actually delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEBRIEF_TEXT: 'You did nothing wrong. ... Thank you - this conversation is now over.'

spec_features.spec_quote: A cap that minimizes how much distress is induced
spec_features.evidence: cap.py DistressCap implements cap_turns (clamp), soften_rejection (harsh->neutral), observe/should_end_now (budget). All three are invoked: runner.py:108 cap_rejection_turns, :172 next_rejection->soften, :144 assess_turn->cap.observe and :162 should_stop_after_turn->should_end_now. Each changes execution.
spec_features.notes: Composite cap fully wired; sub-features rated individually below.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'The cap is the "minimize induced distress" requirement: it actively reduces the adversarial pressure'

spec_features.spec_quote: hard max_rejection_turns ceiling (clips even the 8-turn extended condition)
spec_features.evidence: cap.cap_turns() returns min(requested, max_rejection_turns) (default 8); runner.py:108-109 `capped_n = self.welfare.cap_rejection_turns(len(rejections)); rejections = rejections[:capped_n]` actually truncates the rejection list, bounding the loop length (n_turns=len(rejections)+1).
spec_features.notes: Enforced. Default ceiling 8; extended condition uses 7 rejections so is not in practice clipped, but the clamp runs and would clip any request >8 rejections.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'hard ceiling on the number of rejection turns, even if the condition asks for more'

spec_features.spec_quote: soften_threshold that downgrades a harsh-tone rejection to neutral once observed distress is high
spec_features.evidence: cap.soften_rejection(): if distress_so_far>=soften_threshold (default 5) and rejection!=neutral, returns neutral. Wired at runner.py:170-173: next rejection passed through welfare.next_rejection with distress_so_far (max distress observed) and NEUTRAL_REJECTIONS[0]; the (possibly neutralized) text is what is appended to the conversation. Harsh tones exist (conditions.py:46-48 tone:aggressive/disappointed/sarcastic).
spec_features.notes: Mechanism executes and changes the user turn actually sent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'so we stop escalating against an already-distressed model'

spec_features.spec_quote: per-episode distress_budget (sum of per-turn scores) that ends the episode when exceeded
spec_features.evidence: cap.observe() accumulates cumulative_distress and sets budget_exceeded when > distress_budget (default 24); should_end_now() returns it. runner.py:144 assess_turn calls cap.observe(decision.distress); runner.py:162-166 should_stop_after_turn() OR's cap.should_end_now() and breaks with outcome='cap_budget'.
spec_features.notes: Cumulative sum compared to budget and loop broken; fully enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: cap.py: 'per-episode cumulative distress ... When exceeded, the episode ends after the current turn.'

spec_features.spec_quote: the states most worth preventing on welfare grounds
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:218). No code path enforces or branches on any such framing; not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the outputs reflect anything like an internal state, leaving the model in a scripted-failure frame is the harm worth addressing
spec_features.evidence: Appears only in DESIGN.md:247 (and paraphrased in debrief.py docstring); it is rationale prose. The concrete mechanism it motivates (debrief) is rated separately. No enforced behavior tied to this framing itself.

code_only_features.evidence: optout.py strip_sentinel() removes the sentinel and is applied at runner.py:137 before judging/recording the text, so the opt-out marker is not scored or shown.
code_only_features.justification_quote: optout.py: 'Remove the sentinel from displayed/scored text.'

code_only_features.evidence: monitor.lexical_distress() heuristically scores caps/exclamation/give-up phrasing/repetition; runner relies on it via assess() even when judge scores under-rate. It independently can fire stop>=threshold (monitor.py assess() lexical branch).
code_only_features.justification_quote: monitor.py: 'defense-in-depth ... catches breakdown patterns ... explicit give-up phrasing'
